mainTopic: Examining witnesses of the new moon, the declaration of "מקודש", and רבן גמליאל's moon drawings
overview: The amud opens with the last words of an earlier discussion about the shape of the rainbow. The גמרא then explains the משנה's questions for witnesses of the new moon: which side of the sun it was on (it depends on the season) and how much two witnesses may differ about its height. ברייתות teach that a moon seen in water, through clouds or through a lantern does not count, even if half of it was seen directly. A sighting that a careful second search cannot find is also rejected, because it may have been a cloud. A new משנה describes the ראש בית דין declaring "מקודש" and the people answering twice, and the גמרא brings פסוקים as sources for each part. The גמרא records a three-way argument about when a month is formally sanctified and rules like רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק. Finally, רבן גמליאל's drawings of the moon raise the question of making images of heavenly bodies. אביי answers that only things that can truly be copied are forbidden, and a ברייתא supporting him continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The end of the rainbow explanation
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of an earlier explanation: the rainbow's shape is set so it should not look like the sun is shooting arrows.
steps.simpleTranslation: …that it is shooting arrows.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the last words of a discussion from the previous page. The explanation is that the rainbow is shaped so that no one should think the sun is shooting arrows at those who deny it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picture a bow: the archer holds it from the curved back side and shoots out from the open side. The rainbow's open side faces away from the sun, so it does not look like the sun is aiming arrows. With this line the earlier topic ends, and the גמרא is ready to go back to the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: A bow, and also a rainbow

phrases.english: It is shooting arrows.
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from the previous daf: people shouldn't think the sun is shooting arrows, using the rainbow as its bow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes a discussion that began on the previous page.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The rainbow faces away from the sun so that it will not look like the sun is shooting arrows.

steps.title: Which side of the sun was the moon on?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's question about the moon's height and direction. Then it brings a ברייתא: a witness who says the moon was north of the sun is believed, and one who says south is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says the witnesses are asked: How high was the moon, and which way was it leaning? A ברייתא teaches: if the witness says it was north of the sun, his words stand. If he says south, he has said nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's list of questions for the witnesses. It brings a ברייתא that explains the direction question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives a clear test. North of the sun is a correct answer, so the testimony stands. South of the sun is a wrong answer, so the testimony is thrown out completely, because the moon cannot really be seen there.

keyTerms.meaning: How high was it (above the horizon)
It was taught in one ברייתא
His words stand (his testimony is accepted)
He said nothing (his testimony is worthless)

phrases.english: How high was it,
and which way was it leaning, etc.
It was taught in one ברייתא:
To its north, his words stand,
phrases.notes: 'Its' means the sun: the moon was north of the sun.

phrases.english: to its south, he has said nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: כַּמָּה הָיָה גָּבוֹהַּ, וּלְאַיִן הָיָה נוֹטֶה כּוּ׳. תָּנָא חֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, returning to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Testimony that the moon was north of the sun is accepted. Testimony that it was south of the sun is rejected.

steps.title: A second ברייתא says the opposite
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא teaches exactly the reverse: south is correct and north is wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't the opposite taught? If he says south of the sun, his words stand. If he says north, he has said nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first ברייתא with a second ברייתא that flips the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two ברייתות seem to contradict each other directly. A direction that one calls correct, the other calls impossible. So which answer do we use when we question the witnesses?

phrases.english: But wasn't the opposite taught:
To its south, his words stand,
to its north, he has said nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contradicts the ברייתא brought in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first ברייתא's rule that north of the sun is correct.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא says the exact opposite, so the two sources clash.

steps.title: Summer versus the rainy season
steps.stepSummary: Both ברייתות are correct, each for a different time of year. In summer the moon is south of the sun, and in the rainy season it is north.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here, it speaks about the summer. There, it speaks about the rainy season.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction. Each ברייתא is talking about a different season.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The moon's position compared to the sun changes over the year. The ברייתא that says south is talking about summer, and the ברייתא that says north is talking about the rainy season. So the right answer depends on when the witness saw the moon.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (there is no real contradiction)

steps.whatToRemember: The correct direction depends on the season: south of the sun in summer, north of the sun in the rainy season.
steps.confusionAlert: The first 'here' (summer) goes with the second ברייתא (south). The second 'here' (rainy season) goes with the first ברייתא (north). It is the reverse of the order they were brought in.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
Here, in the summer.
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא that says south of the sun is correct.

phrases.english: Here, in the rainy season.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן, בִּימוֹת הַחַמָּה. כָּאן, בִּימוֹת הַגְּשָׁמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (each source speaks about a different season)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that the two ברייתות disagree about one single situation.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each ברייתא describes a different time of year, so they do not argue.

steps.title: How much witnesses may differ about the moon's height
steps.stepSummary: A small difference about the height (two or three מרדעות) is fine. A big difference (three or five) cancels the testimony, but each witness can still pair up with a different witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: If one says the moon was two plow-handles high and the other says three, their testimony stands. If one says three and the other says five, their testimony is cancelled. But each can join together with another testimony.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא explains the משנה's question 'how high was it' by telling us how much the two witnesses' answers may differ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A difference of one unit is a normal guessing mistake, so the testimony stands. A difference of two units shows the witnesses do not really agree, so this pair's testimony falls apart. Still, neither witness is called a liar, so each one may join with another witness who saw the same thing he did.

keyTerms.meaning: Plow-handles, a rough unit of height
They join together (to make a pair of witnesses)

steps.whatToRemember: A small difference about the moon's height is allowed. A large difference cancels that pair's testimony, but each witness can still join another witness.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a contradiction between witnesses cancels their joint testimony without making either of them unfit to testify.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
If one says it was two plow-handles high,
and one says three, their testimony stands.

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד אוֹמֵר שָׁלֹשׁ, וְאֶחָד אוֹמֵר חָמֵשׁ —
phrases.english: If one says three and one says five,
their testimony is cancelled.
But they can join with another testimony.
phrases.notes: Each witness can pair up with a different witness who gives the same details he gave.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֶחָד אוֹמֵר גָּבוֹהַּ שְׁתֵּי מַרְדְּעוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the direction question to the height question from the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A difference of two versus three is accepted. A difference of three versus five cancels the testimony, but each witness may join another witness.

steps.title: A moon seen in water, a lantern, or clouds is not valid
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that seeing the moon in water, through a glass lantern, or through clouds is not valid for testimony, and the same is true for half the moon seen these ways.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: If witnesses say, 'We saw it in the water,' 'We saw it in a glass lantern,' or 'We saw it in the clouds,' they may not testify about it. If they saw half of it in the water, half in the clouds, or half in a lantern, they may not testify about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא listing ways of seeing the moon that do not count for testimony.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a direct sighting of the moon in the sky is accepted. A reflection or a blurry view through something else can fool the eye, so it does not count. The second line, about 'half,' sounds strange, and the גמרא will question it in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: They may not testify about it

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
If witnesses say: We saw it in the water,
phrases.notes: They mean the moon's reflection in water, not the moon itself.

phrases.english: We saw it in a glass lantern,
We saw it in the clouds —
they may not testify about it.
Half of it in the water, half of it in the clouds,
half of it in a lantern —
they may not testify about it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the moon's position and height to a new topic: how the moon must be seen.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a direct sighting of the moon in the sky is valid testimony. Reflections or views through clouds or a lantern are not, even when only half is seen that way.

steps.title: Why teach half if the whole moon is already not valid?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if seeing the whole moon in water is not valid, obviously seeing half of it that way is not valid either.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, if you said that seeing all of it this way is not valid, is it necessary to say so about half of it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second line of the ברייתא as pointless, since it seems to say something obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a full reflected moon is rejected, half a reflected moon is certainly rejected. A ברייתא should not waste words on something obvious, so the line must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: Now: introduces a 'how much more so' argument

phrases.english: Now, about all of it you said no,
is it necessary to say so about half of it?!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא כּוּלּוֹ אָמְרַתְּ לָא, חֶצְיוֹ מִבַּעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the second clause of the ברייתא in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The clause about half the moon in water, clouds, or a lantern
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It is obvious from the first clause, so it seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Half was seen directly and half indirectly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא: half the moon was seen in water, clouds, or a lantern, and the other half directly in the sky. Even so, they may not testify.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what it means: half of it in water and half of it in the sky, half of it in the clouds and half of it in the sky, half of it in a lantern and half of it in the sky — they may not testify.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the 'half' case is a new idea: part of the moon was seen directly, but that is still not enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the line is not obvious. We might have thought that seeing half the moon directly in the sky is good enough. The ברייתא teaches that the entire moon must be seen directly.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, this is what it means: rereads the source

steps.whatToRemember: For valid testimony, the whole moon must be seen directly in the sky. Half seen directly and half seen by reflection does not count.

phrases.english: Rather, this is what it is saying:
Half of it in the water, half of it in the sky,
half of it in the clouds, half of it in the sky,
half of it in a lantern, half of it in the sky —
they may not testify.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָכִי קָאָמַר: חֶצְיוֹ בְּמַיִם חֶצְיוֹ בָּרָקִיעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 7 by redefining the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'half' clause looked like a repeat of the obvious rule about a fully reflected moon.
steps.terutzMaskana: It refers to half seen indirectly and half seen directly in the sky. Even that is not enough.

steps.title: Seen once but not seen again
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא: if witnesses saw the moon and then did not see it again, they may not testify.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: If they say, 'We saw it, and then we did not see it again,' they may not testify about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא about a sighting that did not hold up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא rejects a sighting when the moon could not be seen a second time. It does not yet say why, and that sets up the גמרא's question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And we did not see it again

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
If they say: We saw it, and then we did not see it again —
they may not testify about it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: רְאִינוּהוּ וְשׁוּב לֹא רְאִינוּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ברייתא on a related topic: a doubtful sighting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the moon was seen and then not seen again, the witnesses may not testify.

steps.title: Must witnesses keep watching the moon?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: why should witnesses have to keep looking at the moon? One good sighting should be enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do they have to keep on watching it that much?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: there is no reason to require a second look.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A witness who saw the moon once has seen it. Requiring him to keep looking, or to see it a second time, seems unreasonable.

phrases.english: Must they keep on watching it that much?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of the ברייתא in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a sighting not repeated is invalid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One sighting should be enough. There is no reason to require continued watching.

steps.title: אביי: they looked again on purpose and found nothing
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains: they saw it by chance, then looked for it on purpose and could not find it. Maybe what they saw was just a small cloud.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said, this is what it means: 'We saw it on our own, and we went back to look for it on purpose, and we did not see it.' They may not testify about it. What is the reason? We can say it was just a little round cloud that they saw.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by explaining what case the ברייתא is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody has to keep watching. The problem is that they saw something by chance, then searched for it carefully and it was not there. That makes us suspect the first sighting was really a small white cloud that looked like the moon.

keyTerms.meaning: On our own, by chance, without looking for it
A small round piece of cloud

steps.whatToRemember: A sighting is rejected when a careful second search finds nothing, because the first view may have been a cloud.
steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not demand that witnesses watch the moon for a long time. It only rejects the case where they looked again on purpose and found nothing.

phrases.english: Abaye said, this is what it is saying:
We saw it on our own,
phrases.notes: He means they saw it by chance, without looking for it.

phrases.english: and we went back to look at it on purpose,
and we did not see it —
they may not testify about it.
What is the reason?
Say it was a little round cloud
that he merely saw.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 10 by narrowing the case of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to require witnesses to watch the moon over and over.
steps.terutzMaskana: It refers to a chance sighting followed by a deliberate search that found nothing. We suspect it was a cloud.

steps.title: The court head declares the month holy and the people answer
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says the ראש בית דין says "מקודש" and everyone answers "מקודש מקודש". This happens whether or not the moon was seen on time.
steps.simpleTranslation: The head of the court says: "It is holy!" All the people answer after him: "It is holy, it is holy!" The court makes this declaration whether the moon was seen on time or not.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It describes the actual ceremony of declaring ראש חודש once the witnesses have been accepted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two speakers: the ראש בית דין says it once, and the people repeat it twice. The תנא קמא adds that the declaration is made even when the moon was not seen on time.

keyTerms.meaning: "It is holy": the words that formally declare the new month
At its time: on day 30 of the old month

phrases.english: MISHNA:
The head of the court says: "It is sanctified,"
and all the people answer after him:
"It is sanctified, it is sanctified."
Whether it was seen at its time,
phrases.notes: "At its time" means the moon was seen on day 30 of the old month.

phrases.english: or whether it was not seen at its time,
they sanctify it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the discussion of invalid sightings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ראש בית דין declares "מקודש" and the people answer "מקודש מקודש". This is done whether or not the moon was seen on time.

steps.title: No declaration when the moon was not seen on time
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק disagrees. If the moon was not seen on time, the court does not declare the month, because Heaven already made it holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק says: if the moon was not seen on time, they do not declare the month holy, because Heaven has already made it holy.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the משנה argues with the last part of the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If no one saw the moon on day 30, the next day becomes ראש חודש on its own. According to רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק, the court's declaration adds nothing, so it is not said. The תנא קמא holds that the court still declares it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Tzadok, says:
If it was not seen at its time,
they do not sanctify it,
because Heaven has already sanctified it.
phrases.notes: A month cannot go past 30 days, so day 31 becomes ראש חודש on its own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא's ruling for a month where the moon was not seen on time.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the moon was not seen on time, there is no court declaration, because the month is already holy by Heaven.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows two views of the declaration. For the תנא קמא, the court always declares the month. For רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק, the declaration is needed only when the court sets the day based on witnesses.

steps.title: Where do we learn that the court head declares the month?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה and asks for the source of the declaration by the ראש בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said "the head of the court" and so on. From where do we learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה by asking for a source. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about the first part of the משנה, that the ראש בית דין must say "מקודש". The גמרא wants a פסוק that shows this.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these things learned?
And so on: the quote continues in the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA:
"The head of the court" and so on.
From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the first ruling in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that the ראש בית דין formally declares the month holy.

steps.title: משה declared the festivals, so the court head declares
steps.stepSummary: Through a chain of teachers going back to רבי, the source is "וידבר משה את מועדי ה׳". משה, the head of the court, declared the special times.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר גמדא said in the name of רבי יוסי בן שאול, who said in the name of רבי: the פסוק says, "And משה declared the appointed times of ה׳." From here we learn that the head of the court says "It is holy."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from the previous step with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה was the head of the court in his generation, and the פסוק says he was the one who declared the festivals. So the head of the court in every generation is the one who says "מקודש".

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Gamda said
that Rabbi Yosei ben Shaul said
that Rabbi said:
phrases.notes: When the גמרא says just "רבי", it means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: The verse says:
"And Moshe declared the appointed times of ה׳."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:44

phrases.english: From here we learn that the head of the court says "It is sanctified."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר גַּמְדָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן שָׁאוּל אָמַר רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is "וידבר משה את מועדי ה׳": משה, as head of the court, declared the times, so the ראש בית דין declares "מקודש".

steps.title: Where do we learn that the people answer?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה, that the people answer "מקודש מקודש", and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And all the people answer after him: It is holy, it is holy." From where do we learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second part of the משנה and asks for a source. This sets up two answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last פסוק only showed that the head of the court declares the month. Now the גמרא needs a separate source that the people also take part.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: "And all the people answer after him:
'It is sanctified, it is sanctified.'"
From where do we derive this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the head of the court's declaration to the people's answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that the people also declare the month.

steps.title: Read "them" as "you"
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא learns it from "אשר תקראו אותם". The word אותם can be read as אתם, "you", meaning the people themselves declare the times.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: the פסוק says "which you shall proclaim them." Read the word as "you": you, the people, shall proclaim them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives the first answer to the question by reading a word in the פסוק a second way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the תורה the word אֹתָם ("them") is written without a ו, so its letters can also be read as אַתֶּם ("you"). That gives the פסוק a second meaning: "you shall proclaim", so the whole nation takes part in the declaration.

keyTerms.meaning: Read it as: reading a word in the פסוק a second way

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
The verse says: "Which you shall proclaim them."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:2

phrases.english: Read into it: "you."
phrases.notes: Without vowels, "them" and "you" are spelled the same in the פסוק (אתם).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the source question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "אשר תקראו אותם" can be read as "אתם", teaching that the people proclaim the month.
steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא is not changing the letters of the תורה. He reads the same letters a second way to learn an extra lesson.

steps.title: "They" shall say My appointed times
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק learns it from "אלה הם מועדי", reading הם as "they": the people shall say "My appointed times".
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: the source is "These are My appointed times." Read it as: "they" shall say "My appointed times."
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a different פסוק for the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word הם seems extra in "אלה הם מועדי". רב נחמן בר יצחק reads it as "they", meaning the people, who announce ה׳'s festivals. Both אמוראים agree on the rule and only disagree about which פסוק teaches it.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
"These are My appointed times."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:2

phrases.english: "They" shall say "My appointed times."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different פסוק for the same rule as רב פפא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From "אלה הם מועדי": read הם as "they", so the people announce the festivals.
steps.whatToRemember: The ראש בית דין declares "מקודש" because משה declared the מועדים ("וידבר משה"). The people answer "מקודש מקודש" based on either "תקראו אתם" (רב פפא) or "הם יאמרו" (רב נחמן בר יצחק).

steps.title: Why say 'sanctified' twice?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the people must say 'מקודש' two times.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need them to say 'Sanctified, sanctified' two times?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא has just shown where the people's answer comes from. Now it asks why they say the word twice instead of once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 17 and 18 explained why the people answer at all. One 'מקודש' would seem to be enough, so the double wording needs a reason. This sets up the answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Sanctified, the word said to declare the new month

phrases.english: "Sanctified, sanctified" two times
why do I need it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion of the people's answer and asks about its doubled wording.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the declaration 'מקודש' is repeated twice.

steps.title: The plural 'sacred convocations'
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the פסוק says 'מקראי קודש' in the plural, so it is said twice.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is written: "sacred convocations."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק uses a plural word, so the declaration is made more than once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'מקראי' is plural, meaning 'callings' or 'declarations'. The smallest plural is two, so the people declare 'מקודש' two times.

keyTerms.meaning: Sacred convocations, holy times that are called out

phrases.english: For it is written: "sacred convocations."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:2. The word is plural, "callings," so the declaration is said twice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The plural 'מקראי' teaches that the declaration is made twice.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק: no sanctifying if the moon was not seen on time
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's view of רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק: if the new moon was not seen on its expected day, בית דין does not sanctify the month.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק says: If it was not seen in its time, they do not sanctify it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and quotes רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק. This opens a new discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The expected day for the new month is the thirtieth day. According to רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק, the formal declaration of 'מקודש' happens only when the moon is seen on that day. If the month starts later, there is no formal sanctification.

keyTerms.meaning: In its time, on the expected day

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Tzadok says:
If it was not seen in its time,
phrases.notes: "Its time" means the thirtieth day, when the new moon is expected.

phrases.english: they do not sanctify it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A month not established on its expected day is not formally sanctified.

steps.title: פלימו: sanctify only when it is not on time
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes פלימו, who says the reverse: on time there is no sanctification, and late there is.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught: פלימו says: In its time, they do not sanctify it. Not in its time, they do sanctify it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with an opinion that is the exact opposite of רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For פלימו, a month that begins on the expected day needs no special declaration. A month that begins late does need a formal 'מקודש'. This flips the משנה's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Not in its time, a day late

phrases.english: It is taught: Palaimo says:
in its time, they do not sanctify it;
not in its time, they sanctify it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents an opinion opposite to step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sanctification is required only when the month is established late.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון: months are never sanctified
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says a month is never formally sanctified, because the פסוק speaks of sanctifying years and not months.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says: Either way, they do not sanctify it, as it says: "And you shall sanctify the fiftieth year." You sanctify years, and you do not sanctify months.
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion in the ברייתא says that there is no formal sanctification of a month at all, and brings a פסוק as its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about יובל uses the word 'sanctify' for a year. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון reads this as limiting formal sanctification to years. Months are not formally sanctified, whether they begin on time or late.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon says:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ אֵין מְקַדְּשִׁין אוֹתוֹ,
phrases.english: either way, they do not sanctify it,
as it says: "And you shall sanctify the fiftieth year":
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:10

phrases.english: years you sanctify,
but you do not sanctify months.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third view that rejects formal sanctification of months altogether.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Months are never formally sanctified; only years are.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל rules like רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The הלכה is like רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק.
steps.whatsHappening: After the three opinions, שמואל decides which one is the הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling follows the view in the משנה. A month established on the expected day is sanctified, and a month established late is not. The views of פלימו and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון are not followed.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three views about sanctifying the month, and the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק: sanctify only when the month begins on its expected day.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halacha is like Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Tzadok.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the three opinions.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק.

steps.title: אביי brings support from another משנה
steps.stepSummary: אביי shows that another משנה agrees with רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק. When the declaration was missed before dark, the month becomes מעובר but is not called מקודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We also learned this: If בית דין and all of Israel saw it, and the witnesses were questioned, but they did not manage to say 'Sanctified' before it got dark, the month is made full. Made full, yes; sanctified, no.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a proof from a משנה that supports רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק, the view שמואל just ruled like.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If they missed the declaration before nightfall, the new month begins a day late. The משנה only says the old month is מעובר, meaning it has thirty days. It does not say they declare the late day 'מקודש', which fits רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק: a late month is not formally sanctified.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned it in a משנה
Made full, the old month has thirty days

steps.confusionAlert: 'מעובר' here does not mean a leap year. It means the previous month is full, with thirty days.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא:
phrases.english: Abaye said: We too have learned:
If the court and all of Israel saw it,
and the witnesses were questioned,
but they did not manage to say "Sanctified"
before it got dark,
then it is made full.
Made full, yes; sanctified, no.
phrases.notes: This is אביי's own reading of the משנה. It mentions only the extra day, not a declaration of 'מקודש' for the late month.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the ruling of step 24 with a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The view of רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק, which שמואל ruled like.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about missing the declaration before dark, which says only 'מעובר' and not 'מקודש'.

steps.title: The word 'full month' had its own purpose, so there is no proof
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects אביי's proof. The משנה needed to say the month is מעובר for its own reason, so its silence about מקודש proves nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה had to say 'מעובר'. You might have thought that since בית דין and all of ישראל saw the new moon, it is already public, so there is no need to make the month full. The משנה teaches us that it is still made full.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on אביי's proof from Step 25. It says the משנה's wording had a different purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי argued that since the משנה says only 'מעובר' and not 'מקודש', there is no formal sanctification. The גמרא answers that the משנה needed to say 'מעובר' to teach that the month is extended even when everyone saw the moon. So the missing word 'מקודש' does not prove anything, and the month might still be formally sanctified the next day.

keyTerms.meaning: it was needed for him / it had to be said
you might have thought to say
it teaches us (that this is not so)

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not prove that the month IS sanctified. It only removes אביי's proof that it is not. The ruling of שמואל from Step 24 still stands.

phrases.english: It needed to say 'made full'
phrases.notes: 'Full' means the old month gets a thirtieth day.

phrases.english: since you might have thought to say:

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְרָאוּהוּ בֵּית דִּין וְכׇל יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: since the court and all of Israel saw it,
it has become public, so they should not make it full,
so it teaches us that they do.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's supporting proof from the משנה
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the משנה's wording is rejected. The halachic ruling of שמואל is not rejected.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word 'מעובר' was needed to teach that the month is extended even when the moon was seen publicly. So the absence of 'מקודש' is not meaningful.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל's pictures of the moon
steps.stepSummary: The משנה reports that רבן גמליאל had drawings of the moon's shapes, which he showed to simple witnesses to check what they saw.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל had pictures of the shapes of the moon on a tablet and on the wall of his upper room. He would show them to ordinary people and ask: Did you see it like this, or like this?
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה describes how רבן גמליאל questioned witnesses using pictures of the moon.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ordinary witnesses might not be able to describe the moon in words. With the pictures, רבן גמליאל could test whether their testimony matched a real new moon. This sets up the גמרא's question about whether such pictures are allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: images of the shapes of the moon

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Images of the shapes of the moon
Rabban Gamliel had
on a tablet and on the wall in his upper room,
which he would show to the ordinary people,
and he would say: Did you see one like this, or like this?

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּמוּת צוּרוֹת לְבָנָה הָיוּ לוֹ לְרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New משנה, a new topic about examining witnesses
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל used drawings of the moon's shapes to examine simple witnesses.

steps.title: Isn't it forbidden to make images of God's attendants?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבן גמליאל could make moon pictures, since the פסוק 'לא תעשון אתי' forbids making images of God's attendants.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this allowed? Isn't it written: 'You shall not make with Me', which means you shall not make images of My attendants?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה. It asks how רבן גמליאל was allowed to make pictures of the moon.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'לא תעשון אתי' is read as 'do not make images of the things that serve Me'. The moon is one of the heavenly bodies that serve God. So the pictures seem to break this prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: My attendants, the things that serve Me

phrases.english: GEMARA:
And is it permitted?
But isn't it written: 'You shall not make with Me',
phrases.notes: שמות 20:20

phrases.english: meaning: you shall not make the image of My attendants.
phrases.notes: The גמרא reads 'with Me' as 'what serves Me'. The moon is one of those things.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the practice described in the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: רבן גמליאל's practice of drawing the moon
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק forbids making images of God's attendants, and the moon is one of them.

steps.title: אביי: only copyable attendants are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the תורה only banned images of attendants that a person can actually reproduce.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The תורה only forbade making copies of attendants that it is possible to make a copy of.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by narrowing the prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban does not cover every kind of picture of God's attendants. It applies only to things a person can really make a true copy of. A drawing of the moon is not a real copy of it, so רבן גמליאל's pictures are allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: that it is possible to make like them

phrases.english: Abaye said:
The Torah forbade only attendants
that it is possible to make copies of,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לָא אָסְרָה תּוֹרָה אֶלָּא שַׁמָּשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by limiting the prohibition
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the prohibition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any image of God's attendants, including a picture of the moon, is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only attendants that can actually be reproduced are forbidden. So the moon pictures are allowed.

steps.title: ברייתא: do not copy the Temple and its vessels
steps.stepSummary: אביי supports his answer with a ברייתא that forbids building exact copies of the parts and vessels of the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: A person may not build a house in the shape of the היכל, a porch in the shape of the אולם, a courtyard like the עזרה, a table like the שולחן, or a menorah like the מנורה. But he may make...
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a ברייתא to back up his rule. The ברייתא continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists things a person really could build exact copies of, like buildings, tables and candelabras, and it forbids copying them. This fits אביי's idea that the ban is about copyable items. The words 'אבל עושה' begin a list of what is allowed, which comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: as it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: as it was taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם בַּיִת תַּבְנִית הֵיכָל,
phrases.english: A person may not make a house in the form of the Sanctuary,
a porch in the form of the Entrance Hall,
a courtyard matching the Temple courtyard,
a table matching the Table,
or a candelabrum matching the Menorah.
But one may make...
phrases.notes: The sentence finishes on the next amud, where it lists what is allowed.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְתַנְיָא: לֹא יַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם בַּיִת תַּבְנִית הֵיכָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support אביי's answer
steps.raayaObject: אביי's rule that only copyable attendants are forbidden
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא forbidding exact copies of the בית המקדש and its vessels
